column1: # doc/forum.org #lineation/shared-lines-table. One row per junction the page
# cannot show, or numeral both witnesses misread. `checked` is filled by Cliff,
# after looking at the page image; the canonical build refuses to use a row
# that is still empty. Folger ids are pointers, never a source of text.
# Rows proposed by src/shared_lines.py (Folger) or written by hand; see reports/regenerate-lr-report.md.

p.852 col.1 prints 39 beside 'Lear. How old art thou?'; miun and trent both read 30. Read as 39 by Claude Code on the miun scan, and confirmed by Cliff on the same scan <2026-09-22>.

Corrected <2026-09-22> after Cliff read the review build. The Globe and the Folger read these lines differently: Folger ftln-2307 'To whose hands' ends there, where the Globe's line runs on '...have you sent the lunatic king?' and turns over, so it is a full verse line and cannot be a displaced second half; the earlier row here, folding it with 'Late footed in the kingdom?', came from matching first words only. The page prints 'Speak.' flush at the margin, an unmarked continuation like V.3 250, and Folger ftln-2308 ends with 'Speak.', grouping it with the lunatic-king line. doc/forum.org #lineation/shared-lines-table records the same wrong match by hand and needs correcting. Image p.866 (miun 00000880): 'Late footed in the kingdom?' flush and short; Regan's line runs the full measure and hyphenates into its turnover 'tic king?'; 'Speak.' is flush at the margin, the same setting as V.3 250's 'Give it the captain.' Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

p.875: 'Come. [Exeunt Lear and Cordelia, guarded.' then 'Edm. Come hither, captain; hark.'; the count needs the fold here. Folger marks 'Come hither, captain. Hark.' ana=#short (ftln-3281), i.e. standing alone. That is not decisive: across the play the Folger marks a half of 41 of our 233 shared lines #short, including II.1.111 'Is he pursued?' / 'Ay, my good lord.', verified by hand against the page in July. See reports/regenerate-lr-folger-check.tsv. Image p.875 (miun 00000889): 'Come.' is flush but its row is filled to the measure by '[Exeunt Lear and Cordelia, guarded.', so nothing could be set after it; 'Edm. Come hither, captain; hark.' follows at the ordinary indent. Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

Folger marks this junction part=I/F; not yet checked on the image Image p.876 (miun 00000890): 'Thou liest.' ends at about a quarter of the measure; 'Edm. In wisdom I should ask thy name;' sits at the ordinary indent and is too wide to follow it on one row. Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

Cliff's decision <2026-09-22>: take the Folger reading. Folger ftln-3550 makes 'Well thought on. Take my sword. Give it the Captain.' one line, so the page's flush row continues it. Note this rests on the Folger's line division, not its @part or its #short tagging, which doc/forum.org #lineation/shared-lines-table does not yet cover. The neighbours corroborate: our 249 'Thy token of reprieve.' and 251 'Haste thee, for thy life.' each stand alone, as Folger ftln-3549 and ftln-3552 (both #short) do. The page alone was ambiguous: the row is flush at the column margin where every other turnover in the play is indented ~2.3u, which had pointed the other way (to a shared half with 'Alb. Haste thee, for thy life.'). Either reading closes the interval. Image p.877 (miun 00000891): 'Thy token of reprieve.' flush and short; 'Edm. Well thought on: take my sword,' at the ordinary indent with the marginal 250; 'Give it the captain.' flush at the margin, the same setting as III.7's 'Speak.' Read by Claude Code on the image <2026-09-22>; `checked` left for Cliff.

p.913 (miun 00000927): Mess. 'Whilst--' / Ant. 'Antony, thou wouldst say,--' / Mess. 'O, my lord!' (displaced). The page cannot show whether 'Whilst--' and Antony's half share a line; the count from 99 to 110 needs a fold here.
column12: Those three rows comprise a single verse line: line 108. The next verse line, 109 is wrapped over two rows.

column12: Junction is split part=I/F; line 10 is Lep. Farewell.

column11: p.922 (miun 00000936): 'Pom. I know thee now: how farest thou, / soldier?' (set justified) / 'Eno.  Well;' displaced. The page prints 80 beside 'Pom. Enjoy thy plainness,', which is line 80 only if 'Well;' is a line of its own (73). The Folger joins them (ftln-1257 ftln-1258).

p.922 (miun 00000936): 'Will you lead, lords?' / 'Cæs. Ant. Lep. Show us the way, sir.' / 'Pom. Come.' (displaced). The page cannot show the junction; the count from 80 to 90 needs a fold here. Not seen on the image.

column11: p.925 (miun 00000939): 'Oct. Sir, look well to my husband's house; / and--' / 'Cæs.  What,' (displaced) / 'Octavia?' set flush, no prefix: Caesar's 'What, Octavia?' continued on a flush row. Alternative with the same count: the Folger pairs 'What, Octavia?' with 'I'll tell you in your ear.' (ftln-1589 ftln-1590).
column12: What concludes line 45; Octavia begins line 46 (finished by "I'll tell you in your ear.")

Folger marks this junction part=I/F; not seen on the image (miun 00000953). Closes 5.1 50 -> 60.

p.941 (miun 00000955): 'Cleo.  Sole sir o' the world,' heads the page, displaced, after 'As things but done by chance.' at the foot of p.940; the page prints 120 beside it, so it is a line of its own.

p.943 (miun 00000957): 'Dol. How goes it here?' / 'Sec. Guard.  All dead.' (displaced) / 'Dol.  Cæsar, thy thoughts' (displaced). The page prints 339 four lines on only if 'All dead. Cæsar, thy thoughts' is one line and 'How goes it here?' another. The Folger joins all three (ftln-3573 ftln-3574).

p.925 (miun 00000939): 'Eno. [Aside to Agr.] Will Cæsar weep?' / 'Agr. [Aside to Eno.] He has a cloud in 's face.', each at the margin after its aside. Schmidt cites the two together as Ant. III, 2, 51 ('Caesar weep? he has a c. in's face'). The Folger sets them as two lines.

p.925 (miun 00000939): 'So is he, being a man.' / 'Agr. [Aside to Eno.] Why, Enobarbus,' at the margin after its aside. Folger part=I/F; Schmidt cites 'were he a horse' as III, 2, 52 and 'he cried almost to roaring' as 55, which leaves room for one line here. Note: at 'Ant. Come, sir, come;' Michigan (1866) prints 60 and Trent (1887) prints 61 (seen on both scans); Schmidt agrees with 61 ('I'll wrestle', 62). The build takes Trent's reading there.

p.923 (miun 00000937): 'Pom. [Aside to Men.] Forbear me till anon.' / 'This wine for Lepidus!' set flush: Pompey's line continued after his aside. Schmidt cites 'what manner o' thing is your crocodile' as Ant. II, 7, 46, one line on.

p.923: 'Rise from thy stool.' / 'Pom. [Aside to Men.] I think thou'rt mad.' at the margin after the aside. Schmidt: 'thou wilt hear me, rise from thy stool' II, 7, 61-62; 'I have ever held my cap off to thy fortunes' 63; 'keep off them' 66.

p.923 col.2 prints 80 beside 'And not have spoke on 't! In me 'tis villany;' (Michigan scan); Trent reads 85. Michigan is ruled out on this page (a reader's pencilled numbers). Schmidt's citations from II, 7, 69 to 118 agree with the count once these rows apply.

p.924 (miun 00000938): 'As his strong sides can volley.' / [stage direction] / 'THE SONG.' heading, set in. The Globe counts the heading: Schmidt cites 'can volley' as II, 7, 118 and 'plumpy Bacchus' (the song's second line) as 121, and the page prints 120 beside 'Come, thou monarch of the vine'. The P4's own Globe <lb> numbering also gives the heading a line. In the P4 it is speech text.

p.942: 'Unpolicied!' / 'Char. O eastern star!' / 'Cleo. Peace, peace!' (displaced). Schmidt cites both 'Unpolicied' and 'O eastern star' as Ant. V, 2, 311; the Folger marks part=I on both and F on 'Peace, peace!'. Not seen on the image.

p.693 (miun 00000707) col.1: 'Dem. Ay, boy, grow ye so brave? [They draw.' / 'Aar. [Coming forward] Why, how now, lords!', both rows full width, so the page cannot show the junction. Counted from the printed 41 ('Go to; have your lath', which Kraken read as 'sheath41'), the printed 51 ('Nor would your noble mother') needs the fold here. The Folger joins the two halves as one line.
p.704 col.1 prints 179 beside 'And cabin in a cave, and bring you up', seen on both scans (miun 00000718, Trent 0720); Kraken reads 176 in Michigan and 170 in Trent.
column12: Human review: the number is 179 in both printings.

column11: p.363 (Trent 0379; Michigan is ruled out on this page) col.1: Gaunt 'And thou--' breaks off and 'K. Rich. A lunatic lean-witted fool,' completes the verse line, set as an ordinary speech row, so the page cannot show the junction. The count from 110 to 120 needs the fold here. The Folger marks only the second half (ftln-0791 part=F), which is why the build did not propose it.

The Folger has no line, but its numbering skips 2.1.290 and ftln-0959 for it.

Your grace mistakes; only to be brief,'). The printed 19 and Schmidt (Mistake 10, Shorten 13, Oppose 18, Castle 20) agree with the count.

The row is set in at the turnover indent (2.4-2.6u), so the build joins it to the row above; the page prints 80 beside 'whether I wake or sleep.', which is line 80 only if both set-in rows are lines of their own (77, 80). p.69 (miun 00000083): 'Claud. Fellow, why dost thou show me thus' / 'to the world?' (at the turnover indent). The page prints 120 beside 'to the world?', which is line 120 only if it is a line of its own; Schmidt agrees (1.2.118 'provost', 122 'I do it not in evil disposition').

p.74 (miun 00000088): 'And what a prisoner.' / 'Lucio. [Aside to Isab.] Ay, touch him; there's the vein.', the aside set flush. The page prints 70 beside 'the vein.'; Schmidt 2.2.71 'your brother is a forfeit of the law'.

p.74 (miun 00000088): 'To use it like a giant.' / 'Lucio. [Aside to Isab.] That's well said.', the aside set flush. The page prints 110 beside 'Isab. Could great men thunder'; Schmidt 2.2.110 'could great men thunder'.
p.76 (miun 00000090): the number beside 'Ang. I think it well:' is a damaged 130, its middle digit broken; both witnesses read 120 (and print 120 correctly beside 'For his advantage', ten lines up).

p.78 (miun 00000092): 'Claud. Now, sister, what's the comfort?' / 'Isab. Why,' (set at the far right). The page prints 60 beside 'speed;', which is line 60 only if 'Why,' is a line of its own; Schmidt 3.1.59 'everlasting leiger', 63 'to cleave a heart'.

p.87 (miun 00000101): 'Our old and faithful friend, we are glad to see you.' / 'Ang. Happy return be to your royal grace!' (displaced, to the measure). The page prints 10 beside 'To lock it in the wards'; Schmidt 5.1.4 'many and hearty thankings', 10 'to lock it in the wards'.

p.88 (miun 00000102): 'Be perfect.' / 'Lucio. I warrant your honour.' (set flush). Schmidt 5.1.82 'pray heaven you then be perfect', 84 'this gentleman told somewhat of my tale', 86 'it may be right'.
p.92 (miun 00000106): 'me to a whore. Your highness said even now, I' -- the 'I' that ends the row is read by both witnesses as a marginal 1. No number is printed there.

p.72 (miun 00000086; and the 1864 first printing, UVa x000027815 leaf 00000090, set identically): the page prints 150 beside 'ask me.', 160 beside 'face?' (the 11th row after it), 181 beside 'Iniquity? Is this true?' (the 31st). Every row is a line, so 181 is exact and 160 is set one row below 'Pom. Doth your honour see any harm in his', the line it numbers. Schmidt cites 2.1.162 'I'll be supposed' and 169 'the house is a respected house', one less than the rows give.

p.99 (miun 00000113): 'Dro. E. Let my master in, Luce.' / 'Luce. [Within] Faith, no; he comes too late;', the second half set at the speaker indent. The doggerel fourteeners rhyme: 'gate?' / 'late;'. The page prints 60 beside 'pair of stocks in the town?', which is line 60 only with this and the next shared line.

p.99 (miun 00000113): 'Ant. E. Thou baggage, let me in.' / 'Luce. [Within] Can you tell for whose sake?', set at the speaker indent; the fourteener rhymes with the next, 'sake?' / 'ache.' (whose halves the page does set as shared).
p.99 (miun 00000113): a stray mark in the left margin beside 'he came, lest he catch cold on's feet.' is read as 19. No number is printed there.
p.99 (miun 00000113): the page prints 90 beside 'Her sober virtue, years and modesty,'; Michigan reads it as 2.

p.109 (miun 00000123; 1864 UVa leaf 127): the page prints 380 beside 'ed me.', the turnover of 'Ant. E. And you, sir, for this chain arrest-', not beside 'Ang. I think I did, sir; I deny it not.', the line it numbers if the Globe's count runs one behind the rows from V.1.237, as its 240-371 and 410-420 do. Schmidt: 'leisure' 375 is the rows' 376.

p.108 (miun 00000122; 1864 UVa leaf 126, set identically): the page prints 230 beside 'He did arrest me with an officer.' and 240 beside 'A needy, hollow-eyed, sharp-looking wretch,', with eleven lines between, none a turnover or a shared half. The Globe's count runs one behind the rows from here to the end of the scene (240-371, 380 set a row high, 410, 420). Schmidt cites 'rabble' 236 ('My wife, her sister, and a rabble more') and 'hungry' 237 ('They brought one Pinch'), so 'Of vile confederates. Along with them' shares a number with a neighbour; which one is not shown, and this row takes the line above.

p.137 (miun 00000151): the page prints 260 beside 'Cost. O, me!' and 290 beside 'ment, to be taken with a wench.', with 31 lines between if Armado's subscription 'DON ADRIANO DE ARMADO.' (set displaced, to the right) is a line. Schmidt cites 'Adriano' and 'Don' at 280, the line 'ments of devoted and heart-burning heat of duty.', and 'damsel' at 292. The Globe numbers the same subscription as a line of its own in IV.1 (p.144, 89; Schmidt 'Adriano' IV.1.89), so this is its own slip.
p.138 (miun 00000152): the page prints 59 beside 'Moth. To prove you a cipher.'; Michigan reads 50.
p.139 (miun 00000153): the page prints 30 beside 'Tell him, the daughter of the King of France,'; both witnesses read 50.

column11: p.141 (miun 00000155): the page prints 250 beside 'eye hath disclosed.', the turnover of 'Boyet. But to speak that in words which his', not beside 'Prin. Come to our pavilion: Boyet is disposed.', the line it numbers. Schmidt: 'disposed' 250, 'love-monger' 254.
p.142 (miun 00000156): 'Arm. But O,--but O,--' / 'Moth. The hobby-horse is forgot.', set displaced; the page prints 30 beside it, which is line 30 only if it is a line of its own.

p.142 (miun 00000156): 'Arm. By virtue, thou enforcest laughter; thy' ends the left column; 'silly thought my spleen; the heaving of my lungs' opens the right, flush. Both witnesses lose 'silly', so the row seems set in at the turnover indent, and starts at 'thought'; the line starts at 'silly', the P4's word the witnesses lost. Prose: every row is a line; the page prints 80 four rows on.

p.144 (miun 00000158): 'Boyet. Who is the suitor? who is the suitor?' / 'Ros. Shall I teach you to know?', set displaced; the page prints 110 beside it. Schmidt 'continent' 111 ('Ay, my continent of beauty').

p.146 (miun 00000160): 'traveller doth of Venice;' / 'Venetia, Venetia,' (set displaced) / 'Chi non ti vede non ti pretia.' (indented); the page prints 100 beside the last, which is line 100 only if the Venetia row is a line of its own.

p.146 (miun 00000160): the page prints 20 beside 'God give him grace to groan!', not beside 'three were in. Here comes one with a paper:', the line it numbers. Schmidt: 'pin' 19, 'in' 20, 'thump' 24, 'bird-bolt' 25.

p.147 (miun 00000161): the page prints 30 beside 'Nor shines the silver moon' (p.146), 40 beside 'My tears for glasses, and still make me weep.', the ninth line after, and 50 beside 'name.'. 40 is set a row high: it numbers 'O queen of queens!'. Schmidt counts forward from 30 ('through' 37) and back from the printed 40 ('keep' 39, 'mortal' 42, 'shade' 44, 'listen' 45, one more than the rows) and is back in step by 'perjure' 47, 'fellowship' 49.

p.153 (miun 00000167; 1864 UVa leaf 171, set identically): the page prints 160 and 171 with eleven lines between ('That ever turn'd their eyes to mortal views!--' / 'Out--' / 'Boyet. True; out indeed.' / ... / 'Not to behold--' / 'Biron. Once to behold, rogue.'), none a turnover or shared half. Schmidt: 'view' 161, 'sun-beamed' 168, 'epithet' 170, so one fold lies between 162 and 168; the page does not show which. This row takes 'Out--' / 'True; out indeed.'; 'Not to behold--' / 'Once to behold, rogue.' is the other candidate.

p.154 (miun 00000168): 'Prin. Will they return?' / 'Boyet. They will, they will, God knows,', the second half set at the speaker indent; the page prints 290 beside it. Schmidt: 'digest' 289, 'lame' 291.

p.157 (miun 00000171): Holofernes' Hercules verses are set with every other line indented, into the turnover band: 'Whose club kill'd Cerberus, that three-headed' is a line of its own. Schmidt: 'imp' 592, 'Cerberus' 593, 'shrimp' 594.
p.157 (miun 00000171): 'Keep some state in thy exit, and vanish.' / 'Judas I am,--' (indented, as the verse is); the page prints 600 beside 'Dum. A Judas!'. Schmidt: 'vanish' 598, 'Iscariot' 601.

p.158 (miun 00000172): 'Arm. The armipotent Mars, of lances the' / 'almighty,' at the turnover indent; the row above is short of the measure, so the build does not join them. The page prints 650 beside 'almighty,'; Schmidt 'armipotent', 'almighty' 650.
p.159 (miun 00000173): the King's quatrain is set with every other line indented: 'To flatter up these powers of mine with rest,' is a line of its own. Schmidt: 'close', 'sudden' 825.
p.160 (miun 00000174): the page prints 890 beside 'Dum. The worthy knight of Troy.', not beside 'Prin. Was not that Hector?', the line it numbers; 900 beside 'Arm. Holla! approach.' is then exact.

p.160 (miun 00000174): both stanzas of Spring set the refrain 'Cuckoo;' centred under 'Mocks married men; for thus sings he,'; the page prints 910 beside the first and 920 two rows under the second, which are 910 and 920 only if each 'Cuckoo;' is a line of its own (the headings 'THE SONG.', 'SPRING.' are not lines). The P4 marks the two halves part=I/F. `line` all: both junctions.

p.160 (miun 00000174): both stanzas of Winter set the refrain 'Tu-whit;' centred under 'Then nightly sings the staring owl,'; the page prints 930 beside 'While greasy Joan doth keel the pot.', which is 930 only if 'Tu-whit;' is a line of its own (and the second stanza is set alike). The P4 marks the halves part=I/F. `line` all: both junctions.
